draft.title: Roman to Integer
draft.statement: You are given a string `s` that represents a Roman numeral. Each character corresponds to a value: `I` = 1, `V` = 5, `X` = 10, `L` = 50, `C` = 100, `D` = 500, `M` = 1000. Normally the symbols are arranged from highest to lowest, and their values are added. However, when a smaller value appears directly before a larger one, it must be subtracted (the only allowed subtractive pairs are `IV`, `IX`, `XL`, `XC`, `CD`, `CM`). Compute and return the integer value of `s`.
constraints: s consists solely of the characters I, V, X, L, C, D, M
s is a well‑formed Roman numeral representing a number between 1 and 3999 inclusive

mentorNotes.keyInsight: When scanning left‑to‑right, a character should be subtracted if its value is smaller than the value of the next character; otherwise it is added.
mentorNotes.bruteForce: Convert each possible Roman pattern to its integer by checking every two‑character combination and summing – O(n) time, O(1) extra space, but with many conditionals it becomes messy.
mentorNotes.optimal: Traverse the string once, using a hashmap to get each symbol’s value and decide addition or subtraction based on the next symbol – O(n) time, O(1) space.
commonMistakes: Forgetting to handle the last character after the loop
Treating every smaller‑than‑next symbol as subtraction, even when the pair isn’t a valid subtractive combination
Using string concatenation or repeated lookups that increase time complexity
Assuming the input may contain invalid sequences, leading to extra validation code
edgeCases: A single character like "V" should return 5
Maximum length "MMMCMXCIX" (3999) tests all subtractive cases
A string where every character is larger than the next, e.g., "MDCLXVI", should be summed directly
